A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConflictVis benchmark and Focus-on-Vision study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine MLLMs, mitigation experiments, predictive-entropy comparisons and failure-case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds human performance, No-type question evaluations, supervised reasoning comparisons and further case studies.

M1.justification: The core NPMI-based benchmark construction and exact FoV prompting instruction remain unchanged. Regrouping four construction stages into three is organizational. Supervised reasoning is introduced as a comparator, while negative-question construction supports an additional evaluation.

E1.justification: v2 newly uses LLaVA-CoT-100k for supervised reasoning training and adds No-type queries with commonsense distractors on existing images. The original 374-image benchmark, action/place coverage, three question types and VQA comparison remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds VR-SFT comparisons for LLaVA-1.5-13B and Qwen-VL-Chat, and Appendix B.5 adds a human reference. VCD, PAI and CoT retain their corresponding comparisons; VR-CoT is the renamed existing CoT baseline.

E3.justification: Added protocols include negative-query construction and image-free acceptance filtering for its MR calculation, a three-annotator human evaluation, and VR-SFT training with three epochs and batch size 256. The original evaluation remains; newly specified generation defaults, prompts and VQA sampling details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a nine-model No-type control addressing the original benchmark's Yes-answer bias. Figure 7 and Appendix D.1 substantially extend attention analysis with image-token heatmaps and contrasting successful and failed cases. Some illustrative failures are replaced. The VQA entropy analysis is retained and relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Predictive entropy was already reported in v1; v2 documents its calculation. The added human accuracies are means across three annotators without variability estimates.

E6.justification: Most matched original scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds No-type accuracy/MR for all nine models, human accuracies of 93.0%, 99.7% and 91.7%, and VR-SFT averages of 80.0% and 81.6% for LLaVA-1.5-13B and Qwen-VL-Chat. These are additional conditions, not same-setting gains over v1. v1 Table 7's general-benchmark results disappear. A new inconsistency appears: GPT-4o place accuracy is 92.9% in v2 Figure 6 but remains 93.0% in Figure 11.

T1.justification: The NPMI and memorization-ratio mathematics are retained despite equation renumbering. Appendix C.2 adds the standard entropy formula to explain an existing measurement; no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion place greater emphasis on diagnosing persistent conflicts and explicitly acknowledge that mitigation remains incomplete. The broad claim about poorer performance on simpler questions is narrowed to Yes-No questions. The benchmark and FoV contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds hypotheses about direct counter-commonsense phrasing in Yes-No questions and accumulating CoT explanations displacing visual evidence. Its new Limitations section acknowledges unresolved root causes, possible training-data bias and benchmark dependence on a single Vicuna probability estimator. These substantially expand the interpretation and qualification of the retained findings.

D1.justification: v2 specifies extraction packages/models, image resolution and quality, model-specific prompts, generation defaults, VQA sampling, mitigation hyperparameters, annotation voting and artifact licenses. These address substantial documentation gaps in v1. However, v1's explicit public code/data statement and repository link are omitted; this establishes lost access guidance, not actual repository unavailability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including ConflictBank, LLaVA-CoT, spaCy and the LLM evaluator-bias study, while dropping the commonsense investigation by Li et al. (2022b) and GPT4Video. Its principal positioning against HallusionBench, AutoHallusion and PhD remains.

P1.justification: Related Work moves before benchmark construction, substantial construction details move into Appendix A, and the experimental appendices are reorganized. The abstract and conclusion are rewritten, limitations and ethics sections are added, and Subjective/difficulty-level terminology largely becomes Open-Ended/question-type terminology.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Introductory and framework illustrations are redrawn, the question-generation diagram becomes a table, and new summary plots, heatmaps and tables are added. Existing entropy and conflict-target plots move to appendices, while the general-benchmark table is removed.

improvement.justification: The No-type control examines an answer-bias concern left untested in v1, while human reference scores, fuller implementation details and explicit limitations strengthen evaluation and interpretation. These provide a useful but bounded improvement to largely retained findings. Omission of the code/data link and small summary-versus-detail numerical inconsistencies partly offset those gains.
